prompt:
High-fidelity desktop application UI comp, landscape 3:2.

SURFACE: the CodexBar for Windows dashboard: a borderless desktop window (landscape 3:2, about 1536x1024) brought forward from the Windows tray. It is an app UI screen (an operate-mode developer tool), shown as a flat, straight-on UI screenshot with no device frame, no photo, no perspective and no people.

REFERENCE IMAGES AND THEIR ROLES:
- Image 1 (gpui-kit Chart gallery screenshot): the CHART AND CARD LANGUAGE to adopt. That means the smooth area charts with soft vertical gradient fills and thin lines, donut charts with a large centre value and small label, inline dot legends at the card's top right, small grey axis labels, generous card padding, and the card anatomy: title, small grey period line, chart, one plain-weight takeaway sentence, then a quieter grey caption. Do NOT copy its light background, its blue colour or its content.
- Image 2 (CodexBar app icon): the BRAND COLOURS. That means dark graphite-navy panels, a glowing cyan bar, a lime-green bar, an amber bar and round status dots. Use those hues as the chart and status colours. Do NOT draw the icon itself as a big graphic. A tiny version of it may appear as the logo next to the "CodexBar" wordmark.
- Image 3 (earlier Editor-Native comp): the STRUCTURE the user approved: a slim title strip, a left rail of views with a Ctrl+K command search, a dense urgency-sorted account table, Chart-style cards for the focused account, and a footer status line. Restyle it with images 1 and 2.

PALETTE (binding): window ground #1E1E2E, panels/cards #2A2A3E, 1px borders #3F3F5F, primary text #E0E0E0, secondary text #9CA3AF. The main chart series is brand cyan #22D3EE, with tints #67E8F9 and #A5F3FC and deep tone #0891B2 for secondary series (one hue family, like the Chart page's blue family). Status colours are used only for state: healthy lime #84CC16, caution amber #F59E0B, limit red #EF4444, and always paired with a text label. The focused/selected item gets a thin cyan left edge. No neon glow overload, no purple gradients.

TITLE STRIP: the small app-icon logo plus the "CodexBar" wordmark at left; view tabs "Usage" (selected), "Spend" and "History"; at right "Updated 14s ago", a refresh icon and a close X.
LEFT RAIL: a "Ctrl+K  Search accounts…" box, then the views Usage (selected), Spend, History, Accounts, Settings.
FOOTER: "8 accounts · 2 need attention · next refresh 1:46".

REAL CONTENT (synthetic demo data; render this text exactly and legibly), sorted by urgency:
1. ChatGPT · Codex (personal): 5-hour window 91% used, resets in 38m; weekly 47%, resets Thu 09:00. Status "Limit soon" (red). Takeaway: "Hits the 5-hour limit in ~25 min at this pace".
2. Copilot · work: premium requests 1,284 / 1,500 (86%), resets Nov 1. Status "At risk" (amber). Takeaway: "On pace to run out Oct 28".
3. Claude · personal: weekly 82%, resets Thu 09:00; 5-hour 64%, resets in 1h 12m. Status "Watch" (amber).
4. Cursor: 71% of included usage, resets Oct 21.
5. Copilot · HemSoft: 612 / 1,500 (41%), resets Nov 1.
6. OpenRouter: $18.42 credits left, $3.10/day.
7. OpenCode Go + Zen: Go 38%; Zen $12.60.
8. Moonshot (Kimi): balance $7.85.
Use a UI sans with tabular numerals. Keep every word spelled exactly. No marketing copy, no invented providers, no empty placeholder cards.


LAYOUT B, 'Chart-first overview': the main area OPENS with one full-width Chart-gallery hero card exactly in the spirit of the 'Visitors' card: title 'All accounts · usage pressure', period 'Last 14 days', a wide smooth multi-series area chart with gradient fills (series in the cyan family, plus the ChatGPT · Codex series in red, with a dot legend top right), takeaway 'Two accounts will hit a limit before their reset', caption 'Highest usage across each account's tightest window'. Below it, a row of four donut cards, one per urgent or near account (ChatGPT · Codex 91% in red, Copilot · work 86% in amber, Claude · personal 82% in amber, Cursor 71% in cyan), each with a centre value, a small status label, a one-line takeaway and a caption with the reset time. At the bottom, a compact dense table of the remaining four accounts (Copilot · HemSoft, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go + Zen, Moonshot (Kimi)) with sparklines.
